title: Shetland lace bottom-up triangle shawl
subtitle: A lace-weight triangle cast on at the full wingspan and decreased in traditional Shetland OXO lace.
excerpt: A bottom-up triangular shawl in lace-weight wool, cast on at the full wingspan and decreased to a neck point, with the body worked throughout in Shetland OXO lace. Wingspan 210 cm, centre-back depth 100 cm. About 250 g of lace-weight yarn. One of the most traditional Shetland shawl constructions.
sourceNotes: The OXO lace pattern is a classic Shetland stitch documented in Sarah Don, The Art of Shetland Lace (1980), §Stitches: OXO Pattern, and in Sharon Miller, Heirloom Knitting (2004). The bottom-up construction with OXO lace is the standard form of traditional Shetland triangular shawls from the 19th century onward.

glossaryTerms.definition: A traditional Shetland lace pattern in which circular 'O' motifs alternate with cross 'X' motifs in a regular grid, named for their resemblance to the letters O and X. Worked on a 12-stitch, 12-row repeat.
A length of smooth waste yarn threaded through all live stitches at a given row. Insert one at the end of each 48-row OXO repeat cycle as a safety checkpoint.

content.text: A bottom-up triangular shawl in lace-weight wool worked in traditional Shetland
OXO lace
from a cast-on at the full 210 cm wingspan decreasing to a neck point. Insert a
lifeline
every 48 rows.

This is one of the most demanding projects in the shawl-wrap category: approximately 290 RS rows total at lace weight, with an OXO pattern that must be maintained continuously through the spine decreases. Budget about 250 g (about 2,000 m / 2,190 yards) of lace-weight Shetland-type 2-ply wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: About 250 g (2,000 m / 2,190 yards) of 2-ply lace-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3 mm (UK 11 / US 2.5) circular needle, 150 cm or longer

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 1 for centre spine, several for OXO repeat boundaries

items.name: Tapestry needle, scissors, blocking mat, pins

content.text: Gauge

28 stitches and 36 rows to 10 cm over OXO lace on 3 mm needles, blocked. At gauge, the cast-on for 210 cm wingspan is approximately 588 stitches (28 sts × 21 = 588; 49 complete 12-stitch repeats). The spine decreases on every RS row reduce by 4 stitches per row; 588 ÷ 4 = 147 RS rows to reach 3 stitches.
Stitches used
Pattern
Cast on

Using the long-tail cast-on over two needles held together, cast on 588 stitches (49 × 12 sts OXO repeat). Tail: approximately (3 × 588) / 10 + 15 = 191.4 cm; allow 200 cm. Place a centre marker after stitch 294. Work 4 plain garter rows before beginning OXO lace.
OXO lace with spine decreases
RS row: k1, ssk, work OXO lace across to 3 sts before centre, k2tog, k1, SM, k1, ssk, work OXO lace to last 3 sts, k2tog, k1. (4 sts decreased per RS row)

OXO lace body (12 sts, 12 rows): Rows 1, 3: k3, yo, ssk, k1, k2tog, yo, k4. Rows 5, 7: k1, k2tog, yo, k5, yo, ssk, k2. Rows 9, 11: k3, yo, ssk, k1, k2tog, yo, k4. WS rows (even): k3, p to last 3 sts, k3.
Continue until 3 stitches remain (approximately 147 RS rows). Bind off the final 3 stitches with a standard bind-off.
Stitch count check-ins
After lifeline 1 (row 48): 588 - 192 = 396 stitches. Each wing holds approximately 197 stitches.
After lifeline 3 (row 144): 588 - 576 = 12 stitches. The shawl is very near the neck point.
Common faults

OXO pattern broken by the spine decrease stitches: the k2tog/ssk at the spine consumes stitches from the OXO repeat. At most row counts this is unavoidable; work the incomplete repeat as plain knit stitches rather than attempting a partial OXO motif.
Cast-on edge too tight to block to 210 cm: cast on over two needles and re-test the blocked gauge on the swatch. The cast-on must stretch to 10% over its resting width under blocking.
Blocking

Soak 30 minutes in cool water. Press out in towels. Pin the cast-on edge aggressively to the full 210 cm wingspan. Pin the neck point. Pin the two sloped edges straight. Leave 24 to 36 hours. Lace weight dries slowly.
Care
Hand wash gently in cool water. Lay flat to dry. Re-block after every few wears.
What to try next

The traditional Shetland finish for a bottom-up triangle is a knitted-on lace edging worked along the cast-on edge after the main body is complete. Pick up one stitch per cast-on stitch along the wingspan and work a 10-stitch deep lace border cast-off perpendicularly.
